text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- French magazine L'Express quotes Algerian guerrillas as claiming that an Islamist organisation was behind an assassination attempt on President Suleyman Demirel in May.

- The officially registered address of wanted crime boss Abdullah Catli, who died last week in a car crash with a top police official, turns out to be a police station. The accident lifted the veil on suspected ties between oragnised crime, police and the state.

- Famous Italian prosecutor Antonio Di Pietro is optimistic that Turkey will fight against corruption as he sees the country more conscious of the issue than it was during his previous visit two years ago.
- Former Interior Minister Mehmet Agar, who resigned after the scandal surrounding Catli's car crash, says he is worried that his successors will not take risks for sake of the state.
- Conservative opposotion leader Mesut Yilmaz says that village guards belonging to the tribe of a government MP, Sedat Bucak, were responsible for the killing of a top casino chain owner.
- Former U.S. Secretary of State Henry Kissinger says Turkey needs a courageous leader to steer it out of trouble. Kissinger was in Turkey to attend a conference held by a businessmen's organisation.
- Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan insists of imposing a maximun price limit of 15,000 TL for bread throughout Turkey despite objections from bakers.
- Turkey will import 4.5 billion cubic metres of natural gas from Egypt.
- One out of eight children in Istanbul suffers from ashtma caused by polution.
